result.topic_en: Gauss reflects on why his attempts to give a concrete (geometric) embodiment of elliptic functions failed: he tried to interpret the elliptic integral as a finite part of a sphere's surface, whereas it probably expresses only an infinitely narrow spherical sector.
result.transcription:
Gauss Math 28 \hfill Fi \hfill (33)
Der Radicalfehler, woran meine bisherigen Bestrebungen, den Geist der elliptischen Function zu verkörpern,
gescheitert sind, scheint der zu sein, {+die Bedeutung, als Ausdruck+}
dass ich dem Integral $\int\frac{d\varphi}{\sqrt{(1-ee\sin\varphi^2)}}$ [-—-] eine[-s-] endlichen Theils der Kugelfläche habe unterlegen wollen, während
es wahrscheinlich nur einen unendlich schmalen Kugelsector ausdrücken soll. \hfill [-157 6/9-]
X 2, 546
G.-Hameln \hfill 7

methods.what: Elliptic integral of the first kind with modulus e, considered for a geometric interpretation on the sphere

items.english: The radical error on which my previous efforts to embody the spirit of the elliptic function have foundered seems to be this: that I wanted to assign to the integral ∫dφ/√(1−ee sin φ²) the meaning of an expression of a finite part of the sphere's surface.

items.quote:
während
es wahrscheinlich nur einen unendlich schmalen Kugelsector ausdrücken soll.
items.english: whereas it probably is meant to express only an infinitely narrow spherical sector.
